body.x: SIONIC AI (CEO SukHyun Ko) announced its participation in CES 2025, which will occur from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas. The company will exhibit at the K-Startup Pavilion.

The company specializes in generative AI technologies and offers its proprietary platform to support enterprise AI transformation. Established in May 2023, SIONIC AI has rapidly gained traction, securing 5.5 billion KRW in investment from multiple venture capital firms and accelerators within its first year. Collaborations with major corporations like Naver Cloud and KT have further accelerated its growth trajectory.

At CES 2025, SIONIC AI will showcase its flagship product, the STORM Platform. This platform incorporates proprietary retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) technology, AI optimization tools designed for non-developers, and advanced data processing capabilities that automate the cleansing and parsing of diverse corporate datasets without manual intervention.

body.cap: STORM Platform’s user interface | Image provided by SIONIC AI

body.x: The STORM Platform enables enterprises to design, manage, and refine AI solutions tailored to their business needs. Flexible deployment options allow rapid implementation of AI models on-premises or across secure and public cloud environments within days.

A SIONIC AI representative explained that their platform empowers clients to build AI solutions suited to their unique challenges, setting it apart from services limited to specific industries. This flexibility has led to widespread adoption across various sectors.

The company is actively expanding its domestic client base while conducting overseas Proof of Concept (PoC) projects to establish market entry strategies and references. By participating in CES 2025, SIONIC AI aims to identify potential partners and collaborators for global expansion. The representative added that they plan to begin their international journey in Japan and Southeast Asia, where their domestic references can be quickly adapted, before scaling to larger markets like North America.

body.x: AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
